summary: Three Indian college friends build brain gaming app Matiks and raise $10 million
detailed: Bengaluru-based educational gaming startup Matiks raised $10 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by General Catalyst, bringing its total funding to over $13.5 million.
Founded in 2024 by Sudhanshu Bhatia, Mohan Kumar, and Sushant Timmapur, the app features mathematics, memory, logic, and puzzle-based games as an alternative to passive content consumption.
Matiks grew to over 300,000 daily active users and 2.2 million monthly active users in September, with users playing 48 million games that month.
The 41-person startup plans to use the new capital to scale internationally, expand its gaming ecosystem, and develop localized experiences and AI-powered game creation.
sentences: Indian entrepreneur Ronnie Screwvala also participated, alongside existing investors Info Edge Ventures, Tanglin Venture Partners and Untitled Ventures.
The latest investment brings Matiks' total funding to more than $13.5 million.
Founded in 2024, Matiks was developed to make mental challenges as entertaining as traditional mobile games.
Bhatia, who has a background in competitive mental maths, began exploring the idea while working on an anti-money laundering strategy at American Express.
“For the last 10 years, the platforms have made entertainment consumption easy, but much of it is brain slop,” Bhatia told TechCrunch.
The founders wanted to offer an alternative to passive scrolling by allowing users to compete in mathematics, memory, logic and puzzle-based games.
Players can practise against computer-controlled opponents before challenging real competitors.
The app also features daily challenges, rewards, quests and streaks to encourage regular participation.
Matiks has witnessed significant growth in 2026, with daily active users increasing from approximately 22,000 earlier in the year to more than 300,000 by September.
The platform also recorded 2.2 million monthly active users in September, during which users played 48 million games, according to Entrepreneur India .
Although most users are based in India, Matiks has attracted players from the United States, South Korea and Japan.

The company plans to introduce localised experiences to strengthen its international presence.

Matiks has begun testing paid subscriptions offering game analysis, practice tools and additional features.
Users can also make in-app purchases.
The startup has introduced Jelo, an experimental platform that allows users to create games for others to play.
Interestingly, despite positioning itself as an alternative to low-quality AI-generated content, Matiks is also exploring AI-powered game creation.
With 41 full-time employees, the company plans to use the funding to expand internationally and develop its gaming ecosystem.
General Catalyst partner Rahul Humayun told TechCrunch that strong user engagement and the team's rapid product development had strengthened the investor's confidence in Matiks.
